lastText: ☰⚙File ClosedA Record Argued For, Not AssumedMinor DefeatItalian High Command, 1939–1945End of hostilities: MAY 2, 1945 · filed out of sequence, pages missingImmediate AftermathArmy Group C surrenders in Italy on May 2, 1945, five days before the wider European war ends: the █████ of nineteen months fighting as a junior Allied partner on Italian soil. The human cost of this path runs higher than the historical one at nearly every hinge point: Italy's own wartime dead, roughly 300,000 military and civilian combined split across two governments and a country ██████ over twice, were already among the higher █████ of any Axis power ████████ to population. Mussolini's answer to Romania was delayed rather than rushed: the single change every honest account of the Greek ████████ says should have been made, and on this path, was. The delay meant to buy Rome a coordinated defense instead bought German intelligence two additional days to reinforce the garrison: █████████ Achse executed even more completely than its historical version. Cremona crossed the Senio at Alfonsine on April 10, 1945 and went on to Venice; Friuli entered Bologna on the 21st beside the Poles; the Nembo's second battalion drove off the German 1st Parachute Division five █████ at Case Grizzano.
